name: Stefan James
tagline: A shy, indebted college dropout who built a self-improvement channel and business online.
startedFrom: He grew up in Vancouver, the son of a Greek father; his family's money fell, he changed high schools three times and was bullied. By his own account he was a C-minus student who barely finished high school, struggled with depression, anxiety and shyness, dropped out of college, and saw his parents go through a divorce and a bankruptcy. In his early 20s he had about $15,000 of credit card debt and paid a friend $500 a month to sleep on his couch.

evidence.claim: He calls the decision to commit his life to self-development one of the first and most important decisions of his life.
At 17 he stopped playing video games and signed up for classes in public speaking, acting and improvisation.
In 2012 he started Project Life Mastery, a blog and YouTube channel to document his attempt to master each part of his life.
Looking back on his credit card debt, he says he first had to take ownership and responsibility for how he got into it: living above his means, not tracking his money and avoiding his statements.
To pay the debt he moved onto a friend's couch for about a year at $500 a month, sold his 1989 Honda Civic for $1,500 and worked weekend construction jobs.
Earning no more than about $2,000 a month, he paid a friend $500 a month to live on his couch and spent another $500 a month on a life coach.
He calls the letter he wrote himself in 2010 a letter of being totally direct and honest with himself, calling himself out on his behaviour.
He says giving taught him to be more generous, and that he started by giving 10 or 25 cents to a homeless person every day because the habit matters more than the amount.
In August 2016 he filmed himself in Nicaragua helping build two houses he had funded, a year after funding one in El Salvador.
Entrepreneur reports, from him, that he helped build schools in Ethiopia, Kenya, Ecuador and India and houses in Nicaragua and El Salvador.
evidence.locator: section 'There is no getting without giving.'

evidence.claim: He names committing his life to Christ as the second of the ten decisions that changed his life, and says his faith made him more giving, forgiving and patient.
Raised Greek Orthodox, in 2019 he went to Israel to be baptized again in the Jordan River and rededicate his life to Christ.
In 2021 he says he has read most of the New Testament and does Bible study a few times a week, though he needs to do more.
He says he has done a morning ritual every day for over 16 years, since he was 17, without checking social media or email first.
While in debt he tracked every expense in a spreadsheet each week, on Tuesdays, and kept to a budget.
In August 2014 he filmed his morning ritual step by step, from waking up to starting work, as an update of an earlier morning-ritual video.

principles.text: Stop avoiding the statements: track every dollar coming in and going out, each week.
Make giving a daily habit, even in small amounts; the habit matters more than the amount.
For any problem, find people who have already solved it and learn from them.
Start the day with your own ritual before you check email or social media.
Be blunt with yourself about where you fall short, in writing if that is what it takes.

quotes.text: It's not how much money you give, it's the habit. The habit is more important than the amount.
You can lose money but you can't lose who you are.
Look at your debt as a blessing, as a gift, as a valuable lesson.

definingMoment.text: On 22 January 2010, sleeping in a friend's living room and in credit card debt, he wrote himself a letter in the voice of his goals for a paid 100-Day Challenge program, blaming his procrastination and lack of discipline; he says parts of it may have come from the program. He later said this was when he decided to commit to mastery. He moved onto the couch, sold his car and took weekend construction work to pay off the debt. Around 2011 he went all in on publishing Kindle e-books, and in 2012 he started Project Life Mastery.

shadow.text: His first big money came from Kindle e-books and from a course on the method, K Money Mastery, which he called his program in a 2015 live stream. A 2015 TCK Publishing summary of an interview with him says he wrote some of the books himself and hired ghostwriters for others. In October 2015 the German trade site OMR reported that he advised buyers to publish health books, such as on gambling addiction, under a pen name posing as a recovered patient, and to report bad reviews as abuse so they disappear; it also reported his claim that e-book sales had bought him a sports car and a $1.7 million apartment. In April 2024 Vox called K Money Mastery 'the OG self-publishing grift course', where a later course seller learned a formula of swapping and buying five-star reviews; Vox does not name him.

screen.notes: A real, living Canadian YouTuber, course seller and coach (Project Life Mastery), not a politician, campaigner or religious founder, with no account of sexual contact with a minor or of sexual violence found; he is in, with a documented dark side around his Kindle publishing course.

review.devilsAdvocate: I attacked all five values against the video transcripts, the blind pick (which shared only Growth) and the press. All five held: Responsibility, Generosity, Faith and Discipline each now rest on three sources, so the blind pick's Mastery, Contribution, Wealth and Determination had no room. The three quotes match his videos' captions word for word. He stays a draft because only one press source tells his life story, an unbylined Entrepreneur profile built on his own account, and no second independent reliable secondary source could be found.
